title: Stress Tests - Federal Reserve Board
summary: This is an institutional reference page describing the Federal Reserve's bank stress testing framework and its evolution from Dodd-Frank Act Stress Tests and CCAR to the stress capital buffer (SCB) requirement. It is not an archiveable document — it is navigational/educational content.
key_points: Federal Reserve stress testing assesses bank capital adequacy under hypothetical recession scenarios using minimum two scenarios
Stress capital buffer (SCB) requirement integrates stress test results with non-stress regulatory capital requirements since 2020
Large banks supervised by the Fed have more than doubled aggregate common equity capital since 2009
Historical components included Dodd-Frank Act Stress Test and Comprehensive Capital Analysis and Review (CCAR)
Page last updated June 22, 2022 — content is historical
why_it_matters: This page is regulatory reference material explaining how the Fed assesses bank capital adequacy under stress. It is not a market-moving document or event and has no relevance to market structure or macro catalysts.
macro_context: Not applicable — source is not a macro catalyst or policy event.
market_structure_context: Not applicable — stress testing is prudential regulation of bank capital, not market structure (trading mechanisms, clearing, settlement, price formation, market plumbing).
important_numbers: $100 billion — asset threshold for banks subject to stress testing requirements
2009 — baseline year from which bank capital has more than doubled
